briefs.headline: Flora's late touchdown sinks West Virginia 45-42 at Iowa State
briefs.summary: Aiden Flora's 2-yard run with 1:57 left beat West Virginia 45-42 in Ames on Saturday after the Mountaineers allowed 577 yards; a DJ Epps fumble with 40 seconds left ended the reply. WVU is 3-2, 0-2 in the Big 12.

briefs.headline: James Madison scores 28 in second quarter, beats Marshall 45-17
briefs.summary: Marshall led 14-10 early in the second quarter Saturday before James Madison ran off 35 straight points at a sold-out Bridgeforth Stadium; George Pettaway ran for 206 yards. The Herd are 3-2, 0-1 in the Sun Belt.

briefs.headline: Ohio holds off Kent State 13-10 after late field goal miss
briefs.summary: Will Hryszko kicked field goals of 40 and 44 yards and Matt Vezza ran 35 yards for a touchdown Saturday in Kent; Kent State missed a 32-yard tying try with 10 seconds left. Ohio is 3-2, 1-0 in the MAC.

briefs.headline: U.S. shuts out Mexico 3-0 in Glendale as Chavez is sent off
briefs.summary: Julian Hall, Cavan Sullivan and Malik Tillman scored in the 28th, 62nd and 84th minutes at State Farm Stadium on Saturday night, ESPN's match data shows; Mexico's Mateo Chavez was sent off in the 67th. U.S. Soccer called it a shutout of 10th-ranked Mexico.

briefs.headline: Bengals elevate Lux and Yeast with Dugger out against Jaguars
briefs.summary: Cincinnati elevated cornerback Bralyn Lux and safety Russ Yeast from the practice squad Saturday for today's 1 p.m. ET game at Paycor Stadium; safety Kyle Dugger and receiver Colbie Young are out, and four players are questionable.

briefs.headline: Rays beat Yankees 1-0 as Rasmussen allows one hit in ALDS opener
briefs.summary: Drew Rasmussen struck out a Rays postseason-record 10 over eight scoreless innings Saturday at Tropicana Field, ESPN reported; in the other openers the White Sox blanked Cleveland 3-0 and the Dodgers beat Atlanta 5-3 behind Tarik Skubal.

briefs.headline: Brewers beat Padres 3-2 after roof cable turns France's drive into an out
briefs.summary: Ty France's would-be go-ahead drive in the ninth hit a roof cable at American Family Field and was caught, confirmed fair on review; Jackson Chourio's two-run homer had tied it in the third. Game 2 is 4 p.m. ET Sunday.

briefs.headline: Yankees leave Judge off ALDS roster for a second straight round
briefs.summary: Aaron Judge, out since Sept. 16 with a right calf strain, is not on New York's 26-man roster against Tampa Bay, manager Aaron Boone said Saturday; Judge "just started running." Game 2 is 8 p.m. ET Monday.

briefs.headline: Bears expected to start Bagent at quarterback against Jets
briefs.summary: Tyson Bagent, who last started in 2023, is expected to start Sunday with Caleb Williams out a second straight game with a Grade 2 hamstring strain, NFL Network reported, per ESPN; coach Ben Johnson has not named a starter publicly.

briefs.headline: No. 25 Missouri routs No. 8 Florida 45-17 behind Roberts' 211 yards
briefs.summary: Jamal Roberts ran for 211 yards and three touchdowns Saturday as Missouri ended a nine-game losing streak against ranked opponents and held Florida to 325 yards; both teams are 4-1.

briefs.headline: England routs Croatia 7-0 in Nations League behind Kane and Saka
briefs.summary: Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka scored twice each Saturday in Rijeka in a match played behind closed doors, with about 6,000 schoolchildren admitted; Kane now has 89 England goals, ESPN reported.

briefs.headline: Hoshoryu makes first appearance since missing the Autumn tournament
briefs.summary: Yokozuna (grand champion) Hoshoryu cut hair at a retirement ceremony at Ryogoku Kokugikan on Saturday and declined to speak; his stablemaster said he has resumed training after knee surgery and plans to join the autumn jungyo (regional tour) partway through, Nikkan Sports reported.

briefs.headline: Fujinokawa, 21, feted as sekiwake with ozeki promotion in view
briefs.summary: Sekiwake (third-highest rank) Fujinokawa, who beat three ozeki (second-highest rank) and won 11 of 15 bouts in September, was honored at a promotion party Saturday where a predecessor said two more double-digit tournaments would make him ozeki, Nikkan Sports reported.

prime.item: The Marine Fisheries recreational limits page, opened this morning at HTTP 200 and marked effective Sept. 2, 2026, prints red drum at 18 inches minimum and 27 inches maximum total length, one a day; its footnote makes any red drum over 27 inches unlawful to possess, and the harvest must be reported to the division. On today's Hampstead tides the drum windows are the last of the morning ebb, about 7:15 to the 9:24 a.m. low, in daylight, and the evening ebb to the 10:30 p.m. low, with the flooded grass around the 3:35 p.m. high in between. The Fisherman's Post October report, posted Oct. 1 and three days old, has red drum as the main inshore target, slot fish with over-slots from the surf and piers, reds schooled in the bays at 22 to 28 inches and better, and reds to 31 inches off Jolly Roger Pier at night.

prime.dates: Open; 14- to 20-inch slot, one over 26 inches
prime.item: A 14- to 20-inch total-length slot with one fish over 26 inches allowed, three a day, per the limits page opened this morning; the harvest must be reported. The shops' October report says the trout are not ready, a few on topwater in the first hour of light, with the water at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, reading 79.5 degrees this morning.

prime.species: Spanish mackerel, king mackerel and bluefish

The October report has Spanish of 14 to 22 inches just outside the inlet with false albacore, and kings to 32 pounds off Jolly Roger Pier.

The reference calendar puts October at the peak of the spot run, and the Surf City and Seaview pier reports have spots and croakers in the evening bottom catch.

sections.label: On the Water

waters.reading: 128 cfs, 1.78 feet at 5:15 a.m., flagged rising against 103.0 cfs and 1.65 feet in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.working: The week-long recession reversed Saturday. The USGS two-day trace, pulled at 5:52 a.m., shows the river flat on its 97.3 cfs, 1.62-foot floor from 2 p.m. Friday to 4 a.m. Saturday, then a slow, even climb all of Saturday with no spike in it: 99.1 cfs at 6 a.m., 101 at 9, 105 at noon, 110 at 3 p.m., 118 at 6, 122 at 9, 126 at midnight and 128 cfs and 1.78 feet from 2:45 a.m. on, every 15 minutes through 5:15. Against the true 24-hour mark, 99.1 cfs and 1.63 feet at 5:15 a.m. Saturday, Saturday's edition reading, that is up 28.9 cfs and 0.15 feet on the day and unchanged over the last hour, so the fetcher's rising flag is right on the day and the rise has paused at the hour; its 103 cfs and 1.65 feet are the first point of its own two-day window, 6 a.m. Friday, not 24 hours ago. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, prime wading water for a sixth morning, now with a third more water than Saturday: the tailouts still cross, the pocket water has current in it again and the fish have the first fresh water in nine days. No water temperature came back from the gauge, and what pushed the river up was not read. At 128 and coming up gently this is still a small-fly river but no longer a 7X one: a 10- to 12-foot leader to 5X or 6X, a size 16 Pheasant Tail or soft hackle on a short dropper under a size 14 or 16 Parachute Adams or October Caddis through the pocket seams and the plunge-pool heads, where a slight rise puts the fish, a size 18 caddis pupa swung at the tailouts in the low light, a size 12 or 14 October Caddis dry alone over the undercuts at dusk, and a small olive or black sculpin stripped tight to the banks at first light while the water carries a tint; a rising river feeds, so the approach can be a little closer and the drift a little shorter than Saturday's.
waters.note: The fetcher's 103.0 cfs and 1.65 feet comparison point is the first point of its two-day window, 6 a.m. Friday, not 24 hours ago; the trace's true 24-hour mark is 99.1 cfs and 1.63 feet at 5:15 a.m. Saturday, Saturday's edition reading, so the river is up 28.9 cfs and 0.15 feet on the day and the rising flag is right; at the hour the gauge has read 128 cfs since 2:45 a.m., so the rise has paused. The fetcher's numbers, flag and read string are printed as written. No water temperature came back from the gauge; the cause of Saturday's rise was not read and is not stated. The Weather Service's active list for West Virginia at 5:52 a.m. returned zero products. Nothing is printed on trout stocking; the DNR's stocking pages carry nothing current.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 24.42 feet at 5 a.m., flagged steady against 24.6 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 24.4 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Saturday's refill drained back out. The trace runs 25.06 at 5 a.m. Saturday, the true 24-hour mark and Saturday's edition reading, 24.95 at 6 and 7, 24.92 at 8, 24.90 at 9 and 10, 24.91 at 11, 24.90 at noon, 24.88 at 1 p.m., 24.92 at 2, 24.85 at 3, 24.81 at 4, 24.75 at 5, 24.72 at 6, 24.66 at 7, 24.62 at 8, 24.68 at 9, 24.53 at 10 and 11 p.m., 24.50 at midnight, 24.60 at 1 a.m., 24.62 at 2, 24.56 at 3, 24.46 at 4 and 24.42 at 5 a.m., five hundredths off the window's 24.37 low. That is down 0.64 on the day and down 0.04 in the last hour, so the fetcher's steady flag is wrong on the day, a six-tenths drop being outside anything it would call steady, and defensible only at the hour. The fetcher's 24.6 is the first point of its own two-day window, 6 a.m. Friday, not 24 hours ago. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access. Upstream the Summersville release held: USGS 03189600 below the dam, stage only, read 11.05 feet at 4:45 a.m. against 11.03 a day earlier and 11.01 to 11.08 all window, and the Gauley above Belva, USGS 03192000, has run 2,730 to 2,770 cfs since 9 a.m. Friday, 2,760 cfs and 4.07 feet at 5 a.m. today, unchanged on the day and at the hour. So the Kanawha's contribution did not change while the pool dropped six-tenths; that is a reading of the traces, not a Corps statement. At 24.4 and easing with the pool back near its floor, the fish are off the current edges and back on the structure itself: shad are the forage and skipjack are with them, so a white or pearl swimbait or a three-quarter-ounce spoon worked across the wing dams, which have less water over them than Saturday and will hold fish on the downstream rock, a blade bait or a three-inch paddletail on a half-ounce head along the riprap at first light, a crawfish-pattern jig crawled down the riprap where it meets the mud for the smallmouth and the drum as the sun gets up, and the lock wall at Byrd as the deep edge for the sauger and the hybrids on a jigging spoon or a live skipjack; with the water settling, slower and deeper beats fast and shallow.
waters.note: The fetcher's 24.6 comparison point is the first point of its two-day window, 6 a.m. Friday, not 24 hours ago; the trace's true 24-hour mark is 25.06 at 5 a.m. Saturday, Saturday's edition reading, so the pool is down 0.64 on the day and down 0.04 in the last hour, and the steady flag is wrong on the day and defensible at the hour. The fetcher's numbers, flag and read string are printed as written; the trace figures were pulled at 5:52 a.m. USGS returned HTTP 503 twice on the parameter-coded request for this site; an all-parameter request answered. The Summersville and Belva figures and their link to this pool are a reading of the USGS traces, not a Corps statement.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 25.64 feet at 5 a.m., flagged falling against 26.18 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 25.6 ft and falling — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Falling, and the flag is right both ways. The trace runs 26.33 at 5 a.m. Saturday, the true 24-hour mark and Saturday's edition reading, 26.42 at 6, 26.39 at 7 and 8, 26.45 at 9 a.m., the crest, 26.39 at 10, 26.34 at 11, 26.42 at noon, 26.38 at 1 p.m., 26.27 at 2, 26.26 at 3, 26.27 at 4, 26.19 at 5, 26.21 at 6, 26.17 at 7, 26.06 at 8, 26.08 at 9, 25.98 at 10, 26.01 at 11, 25.96 at midnight, 25.79 at 1 a.m., 25.92 at 2, 25.78 at 3, 25.73 at 4 and 25.64 at 5 a.m., the window's low. Down 0.69 on the day, down 0.09 in the last hour and down 0.81 from Saturday morning's crest, so the fetcher's falling flag is right on the day and at the hour. Its 26.18 is the first point of its own two-day window, 6 a.m. Friday, not 24 hours ago; the window's high was 26.47. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access. The Gauley release above is unchanged (see Point Pleasant), so this is the reach draining, a reading of the USGS traces. At 25.6 and dropping with the current slackening, the river below Byrd fishes the structure rather than the edges off it: the forage is shad and skipjack with crawfish in the rock, so a white swimbait or a jigging spoon dropped on the downstream face of the wing dams, a half-ounce blade bait along the riprap for the sauger and the smallmouth, a crawfish-colored tube or jig on the riprap in the morning, and cut skipjack on the bottom in the barge cuts and the outside bends for the blues and the flatheads after dark; the lock wall fishes from the downstream side on a live skipjack for the hybrids when a lockage puts current on it, which on a falling pool is the only current there is.
waters.note: This is the gauge below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam, not the tailwater. The fetcher's 26.18 comparison point is the first point of its two-day window, 6 a.m. Friday, not 24 hours ago; the trace's true 24-hour mark is 26.33 at 5 a.m. Saturday, Saturday's edition reading, so the river is down 0.69 on the day, down 0.09 in the last hour and 0.81 below Saturday's 9 a.m. crest of 26.45, and the falling flag is right on both. The fetcher's numbers, flag and read string are printed as written; the trace figures were pulled at 5:52 a.m. No lock notice is printed; the Corps' Huntington District site was not opened.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: high 2:56 AM at 3.5 ft, low 9:24 AM at 0.5 ft, high 3:35 PM at 4.5 ft, low 10:30 PM at 0.8 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: high 1:58 AM at 3.8 ft, low 7:54 AM at 0.6 ft, high 2:44 PM at 5.2 ft, low 9:17 PM at 0.8 ft. Water 79.5F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, observed 5:36 a.m. Moon last quarter, 46% lit, 22.6 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 2:56 AM and 3:35 PM in the sound.
waters.working: A day past the last quarter, 22.6 days old and 46% lit, the moon is at the bottom of the neaps: the gentlest inlet current of the fortnight, with the new moon's springs six days off, Oct. 10, by the U.S. Naval Observatory's table, which answered again this morning. The sound at Hampstead came off a 3.5-foot high at 2:56 a.m. and drains 3.0 feet to a 0.5-foot low at 9:24 a.m., so the last two hours of the morning ebb, about 7:15 to 9:24, land in full daylight; it then fills 4.0 feet in a little over six hours to the day's big water, a 4.5-foot high at 3:35 p.m., and drains 3.7 feet to a 0.8-foot low at 10:30 p.m., in the dark. Those are the four events; none spills past midnight. The surf at Ocean City Beach pier runs ahead: high 1:58 a.m. at 3.8, low 7:54 a.m. at 0.6, high 2:44 p.m. at 5.2, low 9:17 p.m. at 0.8; today's lags from the two tables are 51 to 58 minutes on the highs and 73 to 90 minutes on the lows, the lows again lagging longer, the long-ebb pattern. For the crew's water two miles north of the inlet, tide stage first: the red drum window is the bottom of the morning ebb, roughly 7:15 to 9:24 a.m., in daylight, and again about 8:15 to 10:30 p.m. after dark; the flood through the late morning and early afternoon covers the oyster bars and grass edges and puts the drum in the flooded grass and under the docks around the 3:35 p.m. high; slack at 9:24 a.m., 3:35 p.m. and 10:30 p.m. is dead water. The water at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, read 79.5 degrees at 5:36 a.m., two-tenths under Saturday's 79.7, still a summer number, which is why the shops say the trout are not ready. What is running is three days old, not a month: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry October report posted Thursday, Oct. 1, at 9 a.m. ET, and the feed carried it at 5:53 this morning. East Coast Sports has slot red drum with over-slots mixed in off the surf and piers, Spanish and bluefish plentiful, kings starting to show at the piers, and inshore red drum as the main target, scattered through the ICW, the creeks and the inlets, with no real word on trout; Native Son has mullet everywhere and reds at the docks, creek mouths and grass lines; Spring Tide has the reds schooled in the bays at 22 to 28 inches and better, topwater some days and cut bait others, and Spanish pushing inside the inlet on a high tide; Speckled Specialist has reds on Carolina-rigged live mullet, trout in the first hour of light on a Spook Jr. then live shrimp under slip corks in 15 to 20 feet, and 3- to 4-pound black drum on the bridges and oyster reefs with shrimp; Carolina Flats has big mullet in the ICW, reds on live finger mullet or Gulp under popping corks and flounder as bycatch; Plan 9 has 14- to 22-inch Spanish and false albacore in 15 to 20 feet just outside the inlet on small metal and epoxy jigs. Off the piers, Jolly Roger reports kings to 32 pounds on the bait, Spanish getting bigger, and night bottom fishing for red drum to 31 inches, Virginia mullet, pompano, bluefish, black drum and some flounder; Surf City reports good-sized Spanish on Gotcha plugs, slot and occasional over-slot reds, and evening mixed bags of black drum, mullet, spots and croakers; Seaview reports the mullet migration starting, Spanish and blues on Gotchas or diamond jigs, and flounder, sea mullet, spot, sheepshead, trout and black drum on the bottom. Coastal Angler's Topsail column is still Sept. 1, 33 days old. Setups grounded in that and today's tide: at first light on the bottom of the ebb, cut mullet or a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig fan-cast a couple of feet off the creek-mouth channel edges for the drum, with a Spook Jr. or another walking topwater over the grass edges for the few trout showing; on the long flood from 9:24 to 3:35, a Carolina-rigged live finger mullet, the bait the whole report is built on, along the grass edges and across the oyster bars as they cover, or a Gulp shrimp or a three-inch paddletail under a popping cork drifted along the edges, and a Gotcha plug or small metal jig inside the inlet if the Spanish come in on the high as Spring Tide describes; at the 3:35 p.m. high, the day's highest water, a weedless gold spoon or a soft plastic on a weighted swimbait hook in the flooded grass and under the docks; on the evening ebb, Carolina-rigged cut mullet again off the channel edges for the drum in the dark, and a half-ounce bucktail with a Gulp trailer bounced through the channel edges for the flounder, which are release only; after dark, the dock lights on the night flood with a small white paddletail or a live shrimp under a float for the trout, and a fiddler crab or a piece of shrimp tight to the bridge pilings and oyster rocks on the moving water for the black drum and sheepshead. On the beach, Gotcha plugs and small metal or epoxy jigs for the Spanish on the flooding surf from the 7:54 a.m. low toward the 2:44 p.m. high, under the birds, with the glass minnows the shops describe as the forage and false albacore mixed in outside the inlet; a neap-weak current means the bait pods hold tighter to the beach. The reference calendar lists October as the spot run's peak, with red drum, trout, bluefish, sea mullet and black drum, and the piers' spot and croaker lines fit it. No beach-weather line: the Weather Service's active lists for Coastal Pender and Coastal New Hanover at 5:52 a.m. returned zero products.
